text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Alert detected: multiple containers in us-west-2 showing repeated CUDA OOMs + node flaps. Triggering incident thread.

sre_liz: seeing node-gn3 and node-gn4 flapping, both are running paged-attn allocator. Error surface: repeated `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` then OOM.
sre_liz: stacktrace pasted below from node-gn3:```
E 03:12:41 runtime.cpp:452 allocate_kv_page failed: no free pages (frag_ratio=0.87)
W 03:12:41 cuda_driver.cpp:128 CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at 0x7f34...
I 03:12:42 allocator.cpp:291 attempt_eviction returned 0 pages
```
devon: noticed steady RSS creep on those pods for ~6 hrs before first crash. per-pod graph: +2.4GB over 6h.
cheng: this looks like paged KV fragmentation + slow leak in slab. Evictions not reclaiming due to many small pinned allocations.
maya: customer-facing: two paying customers on dedicated pools in us-west-2 reported 5-15% increased tail latency and a few 500s in last 30m. forwarding logs to cust_ops. cc @cust_ops
cust_ops: flagged to CSMs, they're asking for ETA and whether data exposure risk exists. current impact: request errors only, no logs indicate payload leakage.
eng-runtime-bot: Model fallback engaged for routes using `redwood/gpt-medium:v2` -> degraded to `gpt-small` for impacted zone at 03:25:10 to reduce OOMs.
sre_liz: mitigations attempted so far: 1) drained node-gn4 and restarted runtime container (recovery lasted ~5m then flap returned), 2) increased eviction aggressiveness (no material change), 3) enabled model fallback (reduced error rate).
devon: quick triage commands I ran:```
# check fragment map
redis-cli -h kvmeta-usw2 hgetall node:gn3:fragmap
# force compaction
curl -X POST http://node-gn3:9001/allocator/compact````
cheng: compaction is expensive during peak; it temporarily reduces throughput. compaction returned 70MB reclaimed on node-gn3. not enough.
maya: any customer-visible plan to prevent recurrence in next 24h? they want ETA or workaround.
sre_liz: short-term plan (doable within 30m): 1) keep model fallback on for us-west-2, 2) cordon a subset of nodes and migrate critical traffic to other region (us-east-1), 3) schedule rolling restart of allocator with `--force-slab-defrag` on drained nodes during low traffic window.
devon: note: rolling restart requires operator approval, may cause transient 1-2s latency spikes.
cheng: medium-term: backfill allocator to avoid tiny pinned slabs (we have a patch that groups small pinned allocations into consolidated slabs). can stage canary tomorrow.
sre_liz: customer message draft: "We're seeing GPU memory fragmentation causing increased errors in us-west-2. We've applied model fallbacks and will continue rolling mitigations. No data exposure. Full patch and canary scheduled tomorrow." Thoughts?
cust_ops: LGTM, add contact link and incident ticket: INC-7891.
eng-runtime-bot: health check job reports 3/12 nodes in cluster region showing alloc failures; average token-serving latency up 18%.
sre_liz: immediate action: devon please cordon node-gn4 and start migration of pods to warm nodes in us-east-1. cheng please prepare defrag restart commands and monitor fragmentation metrics. maya keep CSMs updated.
devon: cordoned node-gn4, started pod migration (evict via `kubectl drain node-gn4 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`), moving ~18 workloads. will monitor.
cheng: defrag restart script (dry-run)```bash
#!/bin/bash
curl -X POST http://$1:9001/allocator/prepare_defrag
sleep 10
systemctl restart redwood-runtime
sleep 30
curl -X POST http://$1:9001/allocator/verify_defrag
```
cheng: running verify_defrag on node-gn3 -> reports fragmentation reduced from 0.87 -> 0.63 and reclaimed ~340MB.
sre_liz: good. if defrag on drained nodes yields >300MB reclaim, we can bring them back one-by-one. watch for regressions.
maya: CSMs updated customers, they've pushed back on cross-region failover. want more detail before we migrate their traffic to us-east-1.
sre_liz: acknowledge. alternate customer-friendly mitigation: keep fallback model and enable traffic steering to healthy shards in same region (if possible).
devon: have a rolling plan in k8s to move only non-critical workloads first, that should limit blast radius.
eng-runtime-bot: incident log updated: https://internal.redwood/INC-7891/logs/4989994000
sre_liz: current status summary for handoff:
- Impact: intermittent 500s and tail latency in us-west-2 for ~2 customers (CS reported), ~8% error rate peak
- Root cause hypothesis: paged-attn allocator fragmentation + pinned small allocations causing slow memory creep -> OOM + CUDA errors -> container crashes -> node flaps
- Actions taken: model fallback enabled, node-gn4 cordoned & drained, compaction and defrag restarted on drained nodes (partial reclaim), eviction tuning tried, pods migrated to other nodes, CSMs notified
- Next steps: full defrag rollouts on drained nodes overnight, canary allocator patch for consolidation tomorrow, plan to revert fallback once mem reclaim confirmed
- Owners: on-call (sre_liz) -> overnight owner (cheng) after handoff, devon for node operations, maya for customer comms

sre_liz: handing over to @cheng for overnight monitoring. cheng, ping me if anything spikes >10% error rate or another node flaps. I'm offline at 02:45 PT.
cheng: taking overnight. will keep fallback enabled and run defrag restarts on drained nodes at low-traffic windows. will escalate to @sre_liz if errors >10% for 10m.
maya: noted, will post customer update in the incident ticket and slack channel.
sre_liz: final: add remediation checklist to ticket INC-7891 and include timeline for canary tomorrow 10:00 PT. :white_check_mark:
